idiom_name: net/http: one http.Handler + http.ServeMux + middleware wrappers
implementation_notes: A Go server takes exactly one http.Handler (via ListenAndServe or Server.Handler); http.ServeMux dispatches on pattern - since Go 1.22 including method patterns such as GET /orders/{id} - and middleware is only a function wrapping a handler: func(next http.Handler) http.Handler. What replaces the classic structure: one composed Handler value replaces the FrontController and Dispatcher objects, and per-request state travels in the request or r.Context() instead of controller fields. A custom front-controller interface is unnecessary because net/http's type is the contract that chi, echo and gin also implement.
pitfalls: Middleware order is the reverse of the wrapping order - auth(logger(mux)) runs auth first - so swapping arguments silently reorders the pipeline.
A handler or middleware that returns without writing a response (in particular one that forgets next.ServeHTTP) leaves the client hanging until it times out.
http.ServeMux must not be mutated after serving begins; build the whole mux, including middleware, before ListenAndServe to avoid a data race.
Go 1.22 routing patterns changed precedence rules (method plus wildcard, trailing slash meaning subtree): tables ported from older routers can match differently than intended.
